reader_question: How many people have private health coverage, public coverage, both, or neither, with each region drawn at its true size?
grade_line: Documented: a Census Bureau survey, with its published margins of error
title: In 2025, 213.2 million people had private health coverage and 119.1 million had public coverage, and 23.8 million had both.
measure_line: People by health insurance coverage, millions and percent of the 336.8 million in the civilian noninstitutionalized population, 2025, United States; each area is in proportion to its count
notes: Each circle’s area, and the area the two circles share, is in proportion to its count on one scale; Rule 14.81’s chart draws the same groups with circles of one size.
The four groups are Oath & Action’s sums and differences of the Census Bureau’s published counts, so the margins of error in the table are approximate.

The Bureau counts coverage through an employer, coverage bought directly and TRICARE, the military’s health plan, as private, and Medicare, Medicaid, other coverage for people under an income limit and care from the Department of Veterans Affairs as public.
alt: Three circles drawn at true area for 2025. Private coverage, 213.2 million people, overlaps public coverage, 119.1 million, by the 23.8 million with both, 7.1 percent; private coverage alone holds 189.4 million, 56.2 percent, and public coverage alone 95.4 million, 28.3 percent. A separate circle holds the 28.3 million with no coverage, 8.4 percent.

table.caption: People by health insurance coverage, 2025; the groups are sums and differences of the published counts, so their margins are approximate

notes_internal: Maker A, round 4. Data plan row 118, rule 14.82. Domain D09 (V7 I133). Source line: the derived file's printed line.

Data lead rulings (a) nothing named; (b) three circles at true area on one scale, no frame, the third circle apart by at least its own radius, inks as S87 (1.5 px subject-ink edges, no fill, the overlap in the track ink), the everyone count in the measure line; (c) the grade line. MA-8 and the editor: the title states the two circles and their overlap.

Area check (ruling (b), MA-10): the form finds the distance between the two centers by bisection on the lens formula and fails the drawing where the shared area misses 23,775,140 by more than 1 percent, at every width the build draws and sweeps; the kit's area_of check holds each circle's radius to the square root of its count on the private circle's scale within 0.5 px; maker_a_round4_derive.py --figures, check S88, recomputes the shared area at six radii. The data lead's own read of the SVGs: every area within 0.12 percent at four widths.

Checks by script (maker_a_round4_derive.py --figures, check S88): 213.2, 119.1 and 23.8 million in the title equal the published totals and the derived region, rounded; the regions sum to 336,838,154; every gap between two regions passes its approximate margin.
